findings.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:161: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() requires user != null, preventing passkey form initialization on ordinary login before a user is selected and blocking initial passkey authentication, including for passkey-only users.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: UsernamePasswordForm.java:161: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() requires user != null, preventing passkey form initialization on ordinary login before a user is selected and blocking initial passkey authentication, including for passkey-only users.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem as the golden comment: the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() method requires user != null, which prevents passkey form initialization/UI setup on the initial login page before a user is selected. Both comments point out that this blocks initial passkey authentication (ID-less/conditional passkey login). The candidate mentions 'passkey-only users' while the golden mentions 'first-time passkey login' and 'ID-less passkey authentication', but they're describing the same underlying issue - that conditional passkey UI won't work on the initial login form when no user has been selected yet.
